name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Egyptian urea near $535 a tonne after gas cuts to plants; US retail urea $657 a tonne, up 10% on a year
state: Egyptian urea prices rose to about $535 a tonne amid gas supply restrictions to fertiliser plants (UkrAgroConsult). In the US, DTN's survey for 9–13 Nov, published on 18 Nov, put retail urea at $657 a tonne, slightly lower on the month but up 10% on a year, and anhydrous ammonia at $997, up 16% (DTN). No 60% three-month rise in urea, several exporters restricting at once, or closure of a key export route was found as of 20 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Higher fertiliser costs tend to squeeze farm margins and can feed into food prices over the following seasons.
rubric_hit: Watch kept: Egyptian gas curbs tighten a major exporter's urea supply; urea not up 60% in three months

sources.title: DTN — Retail fertilizer trends, second week of November 2026
UkrAgroConsult — Egyptian urea prices rise to $535 per ton amid gas supply restrictions

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
